body:
Debt-only tender backs Lotte Rental buyout as KB and Woori fund tender; delisting eyed after squeeze-outs

Global private equity fund (PEF) manager TPG, which became the new owner of Korea's No. 1 rental car company Lotte Rental, has launched a tender offer for the remaining shares. The funds were raised entirely with debt. It is a "post-leveraged buyout (LBO)" structure in which the control stake is bought with equity and the remaining shares are bought with debt.

According to the investment banking (IB) industry on the 6th, TPG's Lotte Rental special-purpose company (SPC) Lexicon Korea Holdco borrowed the entire 831.7 billion won in funds for the Lotte Rental tender offer from KB Securities and Woori Bank. The loan agreement was signed on Oct. 27 with a five-year maturity at a minimum fixed annual interest rate of 5.85%.

The collateral is Lotte Rental stock. On Oct. 30, the closing date of the control stake transaction, Lexicon established a pledge in favor of the lenders over the entire 61.17% stake it received from Hotel Lotte and Busan Lotte Hotel. The same pledge is expected to be placed on the shares to be acquired through the tender offer.

The tender offer runs from today through Dec. 3. The target is 14,097,325 Lotte Rental shares (a 38.83% stake) at 59,000 won per share. If all remaining shares are purchased, it will cost 831.7 billion won. KB Securities, which is also a lead lender, is managing the tender offer.

The tender offer price is the same as the per-share purchase price set when TPG signed the stock purchase agreement (SPA) with Lotte Group in August. On the 4th, Lexicon deposited 166.3 billion won of the borrowings into a KB Securities account, and it plans to fill the remaining 665.4 billion won by Nov. 30.

TPG's purchase of the remaining Lotte Rental shares is the opposite of its acquisition of the control stake. At the time of the SPA, TPG was assessed to have beaten domestic strategic investors (SIs) by proposing to pay 1.3105 trillion won using fund capital without acquisition financing.

In fact, TPG is understood to have gained the upper hand by immediately beginning to persuade Lotte Group as soon as Hong Kong-based PEF manager Affinity Equity Partners' bid for Lotte Rental fell through early this year. At the end of May, it won exclusive negotiation rights, outpacing Hankook & Company Group, which had emerged as an SI.

Lotte Group's decision to choose TPG was driven by TPG's plan to buy only existing shares and to invest solely its own capital without acquisition financing. For Lotte Group, whose financial structure had deteriorated to the point of needing to raise guaranteed bonds using Lotte World Tower as collateral, the speed of payment was a key criterion in selecting a buyer.

On Oct. 29, the day before closing, Lexicon secured about 1.2059 trillion won through a paid-in capital increase, issuing 1,205,925 shares at 1 million won per share. Lexicon's 100% shareholder is TPG Lexicon, LP, established in the Cayman Islands, and the general partner is TPG Asia VIII SPV GP.

Analysts say TPG has created a "post-LBO" structure for Lotte Rental through the tender offer. Of the 2.1422 trillion won needed to secure 100% of Lotte Rental, close to 40% will be covered by borrowings. It gave certainty to the seller and, by using the acquired control stake as collateral, reduced the burden of funding the remaining shares.

An IB industry official said, "It is a structure that secures the seller with equity and then, immediately after closing, adds leverage using the control stake as collateral to lift returns," adding, "Once delisting is finished, the ability to set dividends and the financial structure without worrying about minority shareholders is also a reason to hurry the tender offer."

Meanwhile, TPG said it has no plans for a merger, split, or business transfer after the tender offer for the remaining Lotte Rental shares. Regardless of the subscription rate, it plans to buy all tendered shares and then make Lotte Rental a 100% subsidiary through controlling shareholder squeeze-outs and a comprehensive share swap.
